content.text: Inside methods you get a special constant called `self`, which points to whatever instance of the struct is currently being used. This `self` value is particularly useful when you create initializers that have the same parameter names as your property.

For example, if you create a `Person` struct with a `name` property, then tried to write an initializer that accepted a `name` parameter, `self` helps you distinguish between the property and the parameter – `self.name` refers to the property, whereas `name` refers to the parameter.

title: Referring to the current instance
